text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Bosnia's collective presidency considers establishing a central bank and invites the board of governors to participate in the next presidency session to help resolve the outstanding issues.
- Bosnia presidency forms a permanent military committee in accordance to the country's constitution as an obligation taken from the Dayton peace accord.

- Health workers in Bosnian northwestern town of Bihac end a strike started on February 12 over back pays. General strike of Bosnia's Moslem-Croat federation health workers which began March 6 continues.

- Moslem police from south Bosnian town of Mostar fail to remove an obstacle on the road linking Moslem and Croat parts of the divided town, cancelling the meeting of the city council and the office of the High Representative in Mostar, town's Croat mayor Ivan Prskalo says in a statement.
- Bosnia's shadow government "prime minister" Sejfudin Tokic says it will give the country's official government 100 days to prove itself.
- Bosnia's Moslem-Croat federation parliament will hold a session on March 18 to nominate Croat Vladimir Soljic as president and Moslem Ejup Ganic as vice-president of the federation.

- A World Bank mission, led by its Bosnia director Christine Wallich, arrives in Bosnia to hold a number of sessions with the local authorities in order to prepare a programme for future financial assistance to the country in the next two or three years. -- Sarajevo newsroom, +387-71-663-864.
